title: Retrieval evaluation and ranking denominators
outcome: Evaluate retrieval separately from answer quality with explicit relevance grades, duplicate handling and unjudged-document policy.

exercises.title: Separate recall from nDCG
exercises.task: Explain why case A has nDCG 1 but recall 2/3.
exercises.expected: An ideal top two still omits one relevant document.
exercises.answer: nDCG evaluates the quality of the available ranking positions. Recall asks what fraction of all known relevant documents was retrieved.

exercises.title: Return no relevant hit
exercises.task: Rank only the irrelevant document at depth 1.
exercises.expected: Recall, reciprocal rank and nDCG are 0.
exercises.answer: Zero is meaningful here because relevant documents exist in the judged corpus but none was retrieved.

exercises.title: Repeat a document
exercises.task: Put the same relevant ID in two result positions.
exercises.hint: Evidence identity is part of the ranking contract.
exercises.answer: Counting duplicates as new hits can inflate recall or distort position metrics.

exercises.title: Add an unjudged document
exercises.task: Return a document absent from the relevance map.
exercises.hint: Unknown relevance is not proven irrelevance.
exercises.answer: A separate assessment or a declared missing-judgment policy is needed before comparing systems fairly.

exercises.title: Empty relevant set
exercises.task: Evaluate a query for which every judged document has grade 0.
exercises.expected: Recall and nDCG are reported as missing.
exercises.answer: Report the affected query count and its interpretation instead of silently mixing undefined scores into a mean.

exercises.title: Preserve target weights
exercises.expected: They can differ without a coding error.
exercises.answer: The weighting rule defines whose query distribution the result represents; it should be shared by every compared retriever.
